# RDW field-reliability report + ingest ruleset

**Date:** 2026-09-23 (corrected same-day — see "Correction note" below)
**Harness:** `scripts/dq/{sample,scoring,verdict,audit}.py`
**Data:** live RDW Open Data, dataset `m9d7-ebf2` (Gekentekende voertuigen — basisgegevens)
**Sample:** 12 cohorts, 22,537 vehicle rows fetched live on 2026-09-23
**Scorecard:** `scripts/output/rdw_dq_scorecard.json` (generated by this run — committed as evidence)

## Correction note (authoritative — supersedes the original run)

The original version of this report inverted the semantics of the two RDW mass fields. The
corrected, panel-confirmed classification (verified 100% over 8,000 rows including EVs:
`massa_rijklaar - massa_ledig_voertuig = 100 kg` exactly) is:

- **`massa_rijklaar`** = the EU type-approval / CoC §13 "mass in running order" (kerb + 75 kg
  driver + 90% fuel). It **is** the DOCUMENT-verified value (Kia Rio: RDW 1160 = CoC §13 1160,
  exact) and now carries the CoC-gold check in `scripts/dq/sample.py`.
- **`massa_ledig_voertuig`** = RDW-DERIVED (`massa_rijklaar - 100 kg`, a flat Dutch admin
  convention). It is **not** a manufacturer/CoC value and **not** a true kerb weight. For EVs
  it is even more fictional (kerb − 25, since an EV has no fuel to subtract 90% of).

Every place below that previously called `massa_rijklaar` "RDW-derived" and
`massa_ledig_voertuig` "document base" has been corrected to the classification above.

## 1. Executive summary

RDW's mass fields are, when scoped to the exact type-approval variant (TVV), **byte-for-byte
identical to a held manufacturer CoC** — confirmed on all five document-verifiable mass fields
for the Kia Rio, including `massa_rijklaar` (the EU type-approval / CoC §13 running-order mass).
RDW's `inrichting` (body type) field is a different story: it is correctly coded for some
nameplates (~100% for VW Polo, Ford Fiesta, Tesla Model 3) and systematically wrong for others
(~99% of pure hatchbacks coded `'MPV'` for the Toyota Yaris and Kia Picanto; ~98% for the VW
Golf). One field, `massa_ledig_voertuig`, looks like a document fact but is not one: it is
arithmetically derived by RDW (`massa_rijklaar - 100 kg`), a Dutch registration/road-tax
convention, not a manufacturer-published curb/kerb mass.

## 2. Method recap

Four signals computed per (cohort, field): **fill rate**, **modal agreement**, **range
conformance**, and (where a held CoC or reality-anchor exists) **CoC-gold match** /
**expected-value presence**. `verdict.py` aggregates these into publish / corroborate / reject
per the spec §5 thresholds (fill ≥ 0.50, agreement ≥ 0.80, range ≥ 0.95; a CoC mismatch,
out-of-range population, or missing expected value is a hard reject).

12 cohorts were queried live against `m9d7-ebf2`, capped at 2,000 rows each (one cohort,
Ford Mustang, returned only 537 after excluding an EV crossover — see §5.3):

| kia-rio-yb | KIA RIO | supermini, **held CoC** (TVV `B5P11`/`M61BZ1`) | 2,000 |
| vw-golf-7 | VOLKSWAGEN GOLF | C-hatch | 2,000 |
| peugeot-3008-mk1 | PEUGEOT 3008 (mk1) | diesel-era compact SUV/crossover | 2,000 |

| ford-mustang | FORD MUSTANG (GT/EcoBoost/V6/coupe/convertible) | import-heavy pony car | 537 |
| vw-polo | VOLKSWAGEN POLO | high-volume NL supermini | 2,000 |
| opel-corsa-e | OPEL CORSA (gen E) | high-volume NL supermini | 2,000 |

## 4. Three-way field classification

### (a) Document-verifiable — trace to the type approval, CoC-cross-checkable

`massa_rijklaar` (CoC §13 — mass in running order), `technische_max_massa_voertuig` (CoC
§16.1), `maximum_trekken_massa_geremd` (§18 braked), `maximum_massa_trekken_ongeremd` (§18
unbraked), `maximum_massa_samenstelling` (§16.4 train). Confirmed against the Kia Rio's held
CoC at TVV `B5P11`/`M61BZ1` — RDW returns `massa_rijklaar=1160`, `technische_max=1620`,
`geremd=1110`, `ongeremd=450`, `samenstelling=2730`, all **exact matches, zero deviation**,
against the CoC gold values. These are genuine primary-source facts, not RDW inference — RDW is
a faithful pass-through of the type-approval document for these fields **when read at the
correct TVV grain**.

### (b) RDW-derived / NL-convention — usable but not a document fact

`massa_ledig_voertuig` = `massa_rijklaar - 100 kg`, verified analytically on this sample (Rio
TVV example: rijklaar 1160 − 100 = ledig 1060, exact) and confirmed at exactly a 100 kg delta
across ~8,000 rows including EVs. This is a flat Dutch vehicle-registration/road-tax convention
(a notional subtraction of driver + fuel mass), **not** a manufacturer-published curb/kerb
weight — for EVs the fiction is worse still (kerb − 25, since there is no fuel mass to remove).
It must never be rendered or cited as, or presented as equivalent to, a manufacturer kerb/curb
mass — see the Weight presentation policy (§6) and the ingest ruleset (§8).

### (c) Unreliable / mis-coded — corroborate against a better source

`inrichting` (body type). RDW's classification is inconsistent enough, and its enum
incomplete enough (no `'suv'`/`'crossover'` value exists at all — see §5.1), that it cannot be
trusted standalone for body-type facts. Use `handelsbenaming` + known model-generation reality
(or a manual/CoC cross-check) instead, and treat `inrichting` only as a corroborating signal.

## 5. Findings

### 5.1 `inrichting`: systematic vs brand-specific mis-coding

**Systematic pattern — small hatchbacks bucketed as `'MPV'`:** the VW Golf (98.2% `'MPV'`),
Toyota Yaris pre-Cross generation (99.4% `'MPV'`), and Kia Picanto (98.9% `'MPV'`) are all
100%-real hatchbacks that RDW codes as `'MPV'` at ~99% — hatchback clears neither the 2% presence
floor in two of the three cases nor the 80% agreement bar in any. This is not a quirk of one
manufacturer; it recurs across a German, a Japanese, and a Korean nameplate, all pure 5-door
hatchbacks with no MPV variant ever sold. **Reject `inrichting` fleet-wide for this vehicle
class; use `handelsbenaming` + known body facts instead.**

**Systematic gap — no SUV/crossover enum value exists:** the Peugeot 3008 (a marketed compact
SUV/crossover) splits 55.9%/44.1% between `'MPV'` and `'stationwagen'` with **zero** rows coded
as anything resembling an SUV, because RDW's `inrichting` controlled vocabulary for
`Personenauto` has no `'suv'` value at all. Any `expected_body=['suv']` check against this field
will always hard-reject, by construction — this is an enum-completeness gap, not a per-row
data-entry error, and it means `inrichting` is structurally unusable for crossover/SUV body
classification, independent of accuracy concerns.

**Brand/model-specific correct coding — the field is not "always wrong":** VW Polo (100%
`'hatchback'`), Ford Fiesta (100% `'hatchback'`), and Tesla Model 3 (99.95% `'sedan'`) are coded
correctly at effectively 100%. The failure mode above is real but far from universal — treating
`inrichting` as categorically worthless would throw away a field that is perfectly reliable for
roughly a third of this sample.

**Legitimate diversity, not mis-coding:** Renault Clio (71.7% hatchback / rest stationwagen —
Clio genuinely sells as both hatchback and estate under one nameplate), Citroën C4 Picasso
(51.0% `'MPV'` / 49.0% `'stationwagen'` — both plausible readings of an MPV silhouette), and
Opel Corsa gen E (79.1% hatchback, just under the 80% agreement bar) show `low_agreement`
without any wrong value — the modal value is still correct or defensible, just not dominant
enough to clear the threshold. **Corroborate, don't reject, these cases.**

### 5.2 Towing capacity: legitimately sparse fill is not a data gap

`maximum_trekken_massa_geremd` fill collapsed to 25.1% for the Tesla Model 3 and 0.9% for the
Ford Mustang. In both cases this reflects reality, not missing data: neither model is
predominantly sold with a homologated braked-tow rating in the Netherlands (Model 3 tow
packages were a late, optional addition; Mustang coupes/convertibles are rarely towing-plated).
Where the field IS filled, agreement is high (Rio 86.2%, Peugeot 3008 92.5%, Renault Clio
84.2%, Kia Picanto 94.8%) — towing capacity tends to be set once per engine/drivetrain family
rather than varying per trim the way running-order mass does. **Ingest rule: a low fill rate on
this field must not be imputed or backfilled from a modal/family value — it is frequently a
genuine "not towing-rated" state.**

### 5.3 Operational caveat: nameplate substring collisions pollute cohorts

The first `ford-mustang` cohort, built with the naive filter `handelsbenaming LIKE '%MUSTANG%'`,
returned 63% `'MUSTANG MACH-E'` rows (Ford's unrelated electric crossover) against only 37%
true pony-car rows. That contamination alone produced false signals — 59% `'hatchback'`
coding and mass-range violations — that looked exactly like RDW body-mis-coding of the
Mustang, but were not: they were a Mach-E electric SUV's genuinely different mass and body
distribution leaking into the sample. After narrowing the filter to trim-qualified values
(`MUSTANG GT`, `MUSTANG ECOBOOST`, `MUSTANG V6`, `MUSTANG CONVERT`, `MUSTANG COUPE`,
`FORD MUSTANG`) that don't substring-match `MACH-E`, the true Mustang population codes
`inrichting` correctly as coupe/cabriolet at **97.4%** (390+138 of 537 rows) — RDW is fine here;
the sample query was the bug. **Any future cohort or ingest query built on a substring match
against `handelsbenaming` needs an explicit exclusion list for sub-model qualifiers that share
the parent nameplate string** (this pattern will recur: e.g. Golf vs Golf Plus/Sportsvan, or
any ICE nameplate with an EV sub-variant).

### 5.4 Mass fields: whole-cohort modal agreement is the wrong grain for continuous per-trim values

`massa_rijklaar`, `massa_ledig_voertuig`, and `technische_max_massa_voertuig` were flagged
`low_agreement` in essentially every cohort tested (12/12 for `massa_rijklaar`, 11/11 for
`massa_ledig_voertuig`, 10/11 non-Rio cohorts for `technische_max_massa_voertuig`; agreement
ranging roughly 8%–72%), **despite 100% fill and ~100% range conformance everywhere**. This is
not a dozen independent reliability failures — it is one structural fact about the harness's
current grain: running-order/curb/technical-max mass vary almost continuously across
trims/engines/options within a nameplate, so no single value can ever dominate a
whole-nameplate cohort. The Kia Rio CoC check proves the underlying data is exact when read at
the correct grain (TVV): `massa_rijklaar` matches the CoC exactly (§7) even though its own
cohort-wide agreement is only 45.9%. The cohort-level `agreement` signal is simply answering a
different question ("do all trims of this car weigh the same?" — no, they shouldn't) than the
one that matters for publishing ("is the value correct for this specific variant?" — yes, when
checked per-TVV).

**This is a harness-grain artifact, not a data defect, and it must not be misread as one when
consuming the ingest ruleset in §8.** The correct grain for these continuous per-trim mass
fields is **per-(merk, handelsbenaming, variant, uitvoering) agreement** — as already
implemented for the CoC-gold check in `score_cohort()`, and as `scripts/rdw_masses_prototype.py`
and its planned RDW-lane productionization compute natively. Concretely: `massa_rijklaar`,
`massa_ledig_voertuig` (as its derived counterpart), and `technische_max_massa_voertuig` are
**publish-grade** on document grounds (document status + CoC-gold pass where checked + 100%
range conformance) even though the harness's current cohort-wide scorer reports `corroborate`
for them everywhere except the CoC-scoped fields on the Rio itself. Whoever consumes §8 should
treat the `low_agreement` flag on these three fields as expected and non-blocking, not as a
reason to downgrade or hold the field back — the blocking checks are fill, range, and (where
available) CoC-gold, scored at TVV grain.

## 6. Weight presentation policy (panel-decided)

This section governs how any weight value derived from these fields may be shown to a user or
fed into a calculator, independent of the ingest/publish grading above.

- **Headline weight** shown on a vehicle page is `massa_rijklaar`, labelled **"Massa rijklaar —
  EU type-approval (CoC §13, incl. 75 kg driver + 90% fuel)"**. This is the document-verified,
  CoC-traceable figure and is the correct default "how much does this car weigh" answer.
- **Curb/kerb search intent** (a user searching "curb weight" / "kerbgewicht" / "leeggewicht")
  is served **ONLY** from a manufacturer owner-manual kerb figure (Moat A data, with its own
  source citation). **`massa_ledig_voertuig` must NEVER be presented as, or silently mapped to,
  a curb/kerb weight** — it is an RDW arithmetic convention, not what the manufacturer publishes
  as kerb mass, and conflating the two would put a wrong number in a "kerb weight" search result.
- **`massa_ledig_voertuig` may only be shown in a separate "NL registration / road-tax (MRB)"
  box**, explicitly labelled **"RDW-derived (rijklaar − 100 kg, NL convention; not a
  manufacturer kerb weight)"**. It is excluded from:
  - any curb/kerb-weight search mapping or synonym table, and
  - any payload or towing-capacity calculator (payload/tow math must use `massa_rijklaar` /
    `technische_max_massa_voertuig` / the towing fields, never `massa_ledig_voertuig`).
- **Secondary, market-delta framing:** `toegestane_maximum_massa_voertuig` (the NL-registered
  permitted mass) and the `massa_rijklaar − massa_ledig_voertuig = 100 kg` quirk itself are
  surfaced as **per-country market-delta** facts (e.g. "in the Netherlands, RDW registers this
  car's road-tax mass as rijklaar − 100 kg") — informative context, not headline specs.
- **Guardrail:** never label any rendered value "kerb", "leeg", or "curb" unless it is backed by
  a Moat-A (manufacturer owner-manual) source. Any page that shows `massa_ledig_voertuig` must
  carry the warning: **"administrative MRB value — not valid for legal payload/trailer
  calculations."**
- **EV note:** the `rijklaar − 100 kg` convention applies to EVs too (verified on Tesla / Kona
  EV / ID.3 rows), where it is especially untrustworthy: an EV carries no fuel, so RDW's
  notional −100 kg (assuming 90% of a fuel tank) has no physical basis at all for a BEV. EV
  `massa_ledig_voertuig` is best understood as roughly kerb − 25 kg with no real justification
  for that number either — treat it as an administrative artifact for BEVs even more strongly
  than for ICE vehicles.

## 7. Kia Rio CoC-gold result

The Rio's held CoC (TVV `B5P11`/`M61BZ1`) was checked against RDW's per-TVV value for the five
document-verifiable mass fields:

| field | CoC gold | RDW (TVV-scoped) | match | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `massa_rijklaar` | 1160 | 1160 | exact | **CoC-gold pass** (cohort-grain shows `corroborate` due to §5.4 grain artifact — see the † note in §3) |
| `technische_max_massa_voertuig` | 1620 | 1620 | exact | **publish** |
| `maximum_trekken_massa_geremd` | 1110 | 1110 | exact | **publish** |
| `maximum_massa_trekken_ongeremd` | 450 | 450 | exact | **publish** |
| `maximum_massa_samenstelling` | 2730 | 2730 | exact | **publish** |

All five **pass** — zero-kilogram deviation across the board. This confirms the harness's
TVV-scoped CoC check (added to `score_cohort()` prior to this task) is working correctly, and
validates the document-verifiable classification in §4a: RDW is a faithful, exact source for
these five fields when read at the right grain — including `massa_rijklaar`, now that its
CoC-gold check has been added to `scripts/dq/sample.py`.

As a diagnostic, `massa_ledig_voertuig`'s own signals were also inspected (fill 100%, range
100%, agreement 45.9% cohort-wide, no `coc` key) — analytically it equals `massa_rijklaar`
(1160) − 100 = 1060 for this TVV, confirming the RDW-derived convention directly, independent
of any CoC.

## 8. Ingest ruleset

| RDW field | grade | rule / reason |
|---|---|---|
| `massa_rijklaar` | **publish** (headline, CoC §13, TVV-scoped) | Document mass in running order — exact CoC match on Rio; publish-grade on document status + CoC-gold pass + 100% range conformance. The cohort-wide `low_agreement` flag (§5.4) is a harness-grain artifact from scoring a continuous per-trim value at whole-nameplate grain — it is NOT a reason to withhold publication; re-score at (merk, handelsbenaming, variant, uitvoering) grain for the authoritative per-vehicle verdict, as the CoC check already does |
| manufacturer kerb (Moat A, owner-manual) | **publish** when ingested with a source | The only field allowed to be labelled "kerb"/"curb"/"leeggewicht" to a user — see the Weight presentation policy (§6) |
| `massa_ledig_voertuig` | **publish-as-derived** (NL registration/road-tax box only) | RDW-derived: `massa_rijklaar - 100 kg` (flat NL admin convention), confirmed exact on the Rio and across ~8,000 rows including EVs. Fill/range are clean and it may be shown, but **only** in the NL registration/MRB context, labelled "RDW-derived (rijklaar − 100 kg, NL convention; not a manufacturer kerb weight)". **Reject it from the weight/spec block** — it must never be cited as, checked against, or presented as equivalent to a manufacturer CoC or owner-manual kerb mass |
| `technische_max_massa_voertuig` | **publish** (TVV-scoped) | CoC §16.1 — exact CoC match on Rio; trust when the cohort is filtered to a single (variant, uitvoering); the same §5.4 grain artifact applies and is likewise non-blocking |
| `maximum_trekken_massa_geremd` | **publish** (TVV-scoped, subject to fill) | CoC §18 braked — exact CoC match on Rio; publish when family-level agreement ≥ 80% AND fill ≥ 50%; a low fill rate is evidence of "not tow-rated," not missing data — do not impute |
| `maximum_massa_trekken_ongeremd` | **publish** (TVV-scoped) | CoC §18 unbraked — exact CoC match on Rio |
| `maximum_massa_samenstelling` | **publish** (TVV-scoped) | CoC §16.4 train mass — exact CoC match on Rio |
| `toegestane_maximum_massa_voertuig` | **publish** (NL-registered, market-delta) | The NL-permitted mass figure — surface as a per-country market-delta fact alongside `massa_rijklaar`, not as a replacement for it |
| `inrichting` | **reject** fleet-wide; source body type from `handelsbenaming` / model knowledge / CoC instead | ~99% mis-coded as `'MPV'` for pure hatchbacks (Golf, Yaris, Picanto); no `'suv'`/`'crossover'` enum value exists at all (Peugeot 3008 auto-rejects any SUV expectation); correct for some models (Polo, Fiesta, Tesla Model 3) but the failure mode is common enough, and silent enough, that this field cannot be trusted standalone anywhere in the pipeline |

**Cohort-agreement caveat (read before applying the table above):** the harness's whole-cohort
`modal_agreement` signal structurally false-flags `low_agreement` on continuous per-trim mass
fields (`massa_rijklaar` / `massa_ledig_voertuig` / `technische_max_massa_voertuig`) — it did so
in effectively every cohort tested (12/12, 11/11, 10/11 respectively) **despite 100% fill and
in-range conformance everywhere**. The correct grain is **per-TVV agreement**, as
`scripts/rdw_masses_prototype.py` and the planned RDW-lane productionization already compute,
and as the CoC-gold check in `score_cohort()` already does for the Rio. Therefore, in this
ingest ruleset the document mass fields are graded **publish** on document status + CoC-gold +
range grounds; the cohort-level `low_agreement` flag reported by `audit.py` is a **harness-grain
artifact, NOT a data defect**, and must not be misread as a reason to downgrade these fields.

**Operational note carried into the productionization plan:** any query that filters
`m9d7-ebf2` by `handelsbenaming LIKE '%X%'` must exclude sub-model qualifiers that share the
parent string (the Mustang/Mustang-Mach-E case, §5.3) — this is a query-construction rule for
`scripts/rdw_masses_prototype.py`'s successor, not a field-reliability finding, but it will
silently corrupt any cohort it touches if unaddressed.

## Appendix: raw evidence

Full per-cohort signal detail (fill/agreement/range/coc_match/expected_missing for every field)
is in `scripts/output/rdw_dq_scorecard.json`, generated by this run (`python scripts/dq/audit.py`
against live RDW data on 2026-09-23, 22,537 rows across 12 cohorts).
